extracted.intended_audience: researchers invited to peer review manuscripts for F1000Research (open, post-publication reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Performing open, post-publication peer review for F1000Research: reviewers must answer a structured set of questions per article type, select an approval status, and publish their signed report alongside the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the work clearly and accurately presented and does it cite the current literature?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the manuscript is clearly and accurately presented and whether it cites the current literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of the Six Core Review Questions; reviewers address this question in narrative form. Look for clarity of prose, organization, appropriate contextualization, and up-to-date citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the study design appropriate and does the work have academic merit?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the study design is appropriate for the research question and whether the work has academic merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider suitability of study type, controls, sample size, ethical appropriateness, and overall contribution to the field. Answer in narrative form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are sufficient details of methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the methods and analysis are described with enough detail to permit replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for completeness of protocols, parameter settings, software versions, and any procedural steps necessary for reproducibility. Reviewers should note missing details and request additions where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: If applicable, is the statistical analysis and its interpretation appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether statistical analyses are appropriate and correctly interpreted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate choice of tests, assumptions, multiple-testing corrections, effect sizes, confidence intervals, and whether conclusions drawn match the statistical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are all the source data underlying the results available to ensure full reproducibility?
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the source data underlying the results are available to ensure full reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify data deposition, links, completeness, and any restrictions. For data-sensitive fields, note acceptable access controls and metadata requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are the conclusions drawn adequately supported by the results?
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the authors' conclusions are justified by the presented results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for overinterpretation, unsupported causal claims, speculative language, and consistency between results, discussion, and stated limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status — Approved
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer judges the article scientifically sound and ready for indexing without further revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting 'Approved' indicates no required changes. Reports should still note minor suggestions if desired, and include explicit justification for the approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status — Approved with Reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: Article has academic merit but requires changes (small or significant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer must enumerate the required changes. Distinguish required versus suggested changes in the report and be specific so authors can respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status — Not Approved
rubrics_metrics.description: Article has fundamental flaws that make it unsuitable for indexing in current form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer must justify the decision with specific concerns. Explain whether flaws are remediable and what would be required for future approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing/pass criteria based on reviewer approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper is eligible for indexing (PubMed, Scopus, etc.) when it has either two Approved statuses OR one Approved + two Approved with Reservations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit policy rule determining when a paper passes peer review for indexing; reviewers' selections contribute to this threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility — doctoral or equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer should hold a PhD/MD/MBBS or equivalent doctorate (with industry/publication-history alternatives where doctorates are less common).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility also considers field norms; when doctorates are uncommon, demonstrated professional experience/publication history may substitute. Journals may require documented qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility — demonstrable experience in the same field
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer must have demonstrable experience in the same field as the article topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience is assessed via publication history, technical expertise, and familiarity with the methods and literature relevant to the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility — lead authorship requirement for some areas
rubrics_metrics.description: For some subject areas, reviewers should have lead authorship on at least three publications in the past five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a subject-area-specific stronger eligibility requirement intended to ensure recent, active expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility — impartiality and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must be impartial and disclose any competing interests (financial or non-financial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts should be declared up front; significant competing interests may preclude reviewing. See conduct norms for how to state competing interests in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method Articles — emphasis on reproducibility, validation, applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: For Method Articles, reviewers should emphasise reproducibility of the protocol, validation, and applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that protocols are sufficiently detailed, validated on realistic data/samples, and that scope/limitations are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software Tool Articles — emphasis on software design, code availability, documentation, testing
rubrics_metrics.description: For Software Tool Articles, reviewers should assess software design, code availability, documentation, and testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify code access (repositories, licenses), installation instructions, example workflows, test coverage, and suitability for intended users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Notes — emphasis on data quality, availability, format, metadata, FAIR compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: For Data Notes, reviewers should emphasise data quality, availability, format, metadata, and FAIR compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess completeness of metadata, adherence to community standards, persistent identifiers, and accessibility for reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic Reviews — PRISMA compliance, search comprehensiveness, RoB assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: For Systematic Reviews, reviewers should check PRISMA compliance, comprehensiveness of searches, and risk-of-bias assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate search strategies, inclusion/exclusion criteria, study selection transparency, and appropriate risk-of-bias tools and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Reports — CARE-statement compliance, clinical relevance, informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: For Case Reports, reviewers should assess CARE-statement compliance, clinical relevance, and informed consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that patient consent/ethical considerations are documented and that the report follows CARE guidelines for case reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Protocols — clarity of objectives, soundness of methods, ethical clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: For Study Protocols, reviewers should evaluate clarity of objectives, soundness of methods, and evidence of ethical clearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine planned analyses, sample size justification, feasibility, and whether ethics approval or registry entry is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct — open identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer's name and affiliation are published with the report (open identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reviews are signed and public, reviewers should be aware their comments will be associated with their identity and held to public standards of professionalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct — constructive tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should use a constructive tone that helps the author improve the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ad hominem or dismissive language; focus on actionable suggestions and clear explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct — substantive specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticisms should be tied to specific sections, sentences, or data points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite exact locations (e.g., figure/table/line/section) so authors can respond point-by-point and make targeted revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct — no coercive citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not coerce citation of the reviewer's own work unless it is directly relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to cite the reviewer's publications must be justified by relevance to the manuscript; avoid self-promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct — declared competing interests in report
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an explicit statement of any competing interests at the head of the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State financial and non-financial conflicts clearly so readers and editors can assess potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct — independence (no close collaborators or same-institution reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not review papers from your own institution or close collaborators to preserve independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt about the closeness of a relationship, disclose it and consult the editor; recuse when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report structure — one-paragraph summary demonstrating understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the report with a one-paragraph summary of the article to demonstrate the reviewer has read and understood the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise summary helps authors and readers see the reviewer's perspective and frames subsequent comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report structure — organise substantive comments by category
rubrics_metrics.description: Organise substantive comments by category (design, methods, analysis, presentation, conclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouping comments helps authors address related issues together and makes responses clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report structure — numbered specific points
rubrics_metrics.description: List numbered specific points so the author can respond point-by-point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering facilitates clear author responses and editorial handling of revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report structure — distinguish required vs suggested changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly distinguish required changes from suggested (optional) changes in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label items as 'required' (must be addressed for approval) versus 'suggested' (improvements or optional clarifications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report structure — include approval status with explicit justification
rubrics_metrics.description: State the approval status (Approved / Approved with Reservations / Not Approved) and provide explicit justification for the selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification should reference specific points in the report and, for 'Approved with Reservations' or 'Not Approved', enumerate required changes or fundamental concerns.
